content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary of the review (Rule IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data):**

- **Favourable and left alone:** Section 11.1.1.1 (each Party retains its pre-Effective Date IP), Section 11.1.1.3 (PB is sole owner of all Trial Inventions, with SFJ assigning and flowing the obligation down to affiliates, consultants and Permitted Third Parties), Section 2.5.1.1 (PB retains ownership of Background Materials), Section 11.2/11.3 (PB controls prosecution and enforcement). No joint-ownership construct exists anywhere. PB's outright ownership of the work product exceeds the fallback licence elements.
- **Deviation found:** Section 11.1.1.4 vests **sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package, including all Research Results — i.e. all data generated in our clinical programme — in SFJ**, with PB obliged to repurchase it (priced at Article 6 §6.1 and the Article 14 termination buy-backs). Vesting Customer Data in the counterparty is walk-away territory under this rule and goes well beyond any processing licence.
- **Redline (fallback level, minimality gate passed):** three surgical edits inside §11.1.1.4 — ownership flipped to PB, SFJ confined to processing the data solely to perform its obligations, SFJ's present assignment substituted for the "sell and transfer" mechanic, and the Exhibit K step reframed as confirming PB's ownership. Payment consideration, the Exhibit K trigger events, and the §14.3.1 backstop assignment are preserved so no cross-reference is left dangling.
